title: introduce-turnwise-behavioral-drift-guard-ci-adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a turnwise behavioral drift CI adapter that computes a per-turn consistency score and fails PRs when weighted regression exceeds configurable thresholds. Includes unit tests and a lightweight GitHub Actions smoke workflow.
description:
Motivation: Multi-turn prompt sets can mask regressions when only aggregate single-turn metrics are measured. Teams shipping chat/assistant experiences need a CI guard that reasons about changes to behavior across turns (turn i -> turn i+1), not just per-turn aggregates. This PR introduces a Turnwise Behavioral Drift Guard: a CI adapter and evaluation metric that (1) computes a turn-consistency-score across prompt sets, (2) produces a per-turn delta heatmap for quick triage, and (3) plugs into existing eval-harness CI gates to fail CI when drift exceeds configured tolerances.

What this PR includes (single-string description): - New metric: turn_consistency_score (range 0..1, higher is better). It blends semantic similarity, length-normalized token overlap, and a turn-indexed coherence term. - Drift adapter: eval_harness/hooks/turnwise_guard.py implementing a pluggable CI adapter that emits structured signal for the CI gate. - Threshold config: eval_harness/configs/turnwise_guard.yaml with default soft/hard thresholds per severity and per-turn-weighting presets (short/medium/long dialogues). - Tests: tests/unit/test_turnwise_guard.py with deterministic seeds and synthetic multi-turn fixtures. - Docs: docs/ci_hooks/turnwise-drift-guard.md explaining interpretation, thresholds, and recommended remediation steps. - Examples: examples/prompt_sets/turnwise_simulated.yaml demonstrating how to author multi-turn probes for conversational features. - CI: .github/workflows/turnwise-smoke.yml — a lightweight smoke job that runs the adapter against a small anchor set and verifies no unexpected failures on PRs.

Checklist (completed): [x] Implementation of core metric and adapter. [x] Unit tests covering positive/negative drift cases and edge behaviors (single-turn fallback, missing turn histories). [x] Deterministic sampling seeds for test stability. [x] Docs + example prompt sets. [x] GitHub Actions smoke workflow and ci gating integration.

Commits summary: - 1f3b9a0: initial turn_consistency_score prototype and CLI harness. - 2c9d8f4: add CI adapter scaffold and adapter-to-gate plumbing. - 6aa7e2e: add unit tests and deterministic seed utilities. - 8c2b71d: docs, examples, and config presets. - bf9d3c1: address review feedback (edge-case handling, additional metrics emitted).

Files changed (high level): - eval_harness/hooks/turnwise_guard.py (new): core adapter + metric computation and exporter hooks. - eval_harness/metrics/turn_metrics.py (new): reusable turnwise primitives and similarity aggregators. - tests/unit/test_turnwise_guard.py (new): 12 test cases covering stability and regression scenarios. - docs/ci_hooks/turnwise-drift-guard.md (new): how-to and thresholds. - examples/prompt_sets/turnwise_simulated.yaml (new): synthetic multi-turn probe definitions. - .github/workflows/turnwise-smoke.yml (new): CI smoke job.

Review conversation (condensed into a single string): Reviewer Ethan Martinez: "Great direction — can you make the test fixtures deterministic and add a minimal stress test for >5-turn dialogues? Also please surface per-turn token counts in the emitted telemetry." Author (Maya Chen): "Added deterministic-seed helper and expanded fixtures to include a 7-turn stress case; token counts included in metric payload. See commit 6aa7e2e." Reviewer Priya Rao: "We should avoid failing CI for tiny sample sizes by default. Can we add a minimum effective-sample-size check and a soft-fail mode with annotation?" Author: "Added min_sample_size config and soft-fail mode. Default config is conservative (soft threshold first) and the adapter emits a recommendation explaining the reason for soft-fail." Reviewer Jonas Berg: "Naming nit: turn_consistency_score -> turnwise_consistency_score? Also provide a small explainer in docs about how the weighting across turns is computed." Author: "Kept turn_consistency_score for backwards-compat with metric naming conventions in the harness, added extended explanation and a worked example in docs. Resolved comments and pushed fixups."

CI details (compressed): - Initial run: lint failed (line-length in docs), fixed in 8c2b71d. - Unit tests: two intermittent flakes in similarity comparator on CI; traced to nondeterministic RNG in a helper; deterministic-seed helper added and tests re-run. - Integration smoke job: passed on rerun. Final CI state: all checks passing.

Why this is different from existing eval gates: existing gates focus on per-prompt aggregates, cohort stability, and semantic anchors. This guard is explicitly turn-index-aware: it detects regressions that manifest as changes in how the model responds in later turns given earlier context (e.g., maintaining persona, consistent facts across turns, or context carry-forward). That makes it particularly useful for assistant/chat features and multi-turn rerankers.

Operational notes and rollout plan: - Default config uses soft-fail to annotate PRs on first detection; teams can opt into hard-fail in their repo-level config. - We recommend enabling the smoke workflow on main for any repositories that exercise multi-turn flows in prod. - We added a runbook section in docs/ci_hooks/turnwise-drift-guard.md covering triage flows, example thresholds, and rollback suggestions.

Related: ENG-5342 (project to harden multi-turn evals), ENG-5410 (pilot integration with console alerting).
